note: The testcase bytes are copied verbatim into the buffer the parser reads.
The fuzzing path intentionally trims one byte from the reported input length.
The lexer uses the shortened length as its exclusive end pointer.
A leading triple quote causes the lexer to enter multiline-string scanning.
The scanner chooses a three-byte terminator and immediately inspects the next byte after the opener.
Each loop iteration compares three bytes at the current position before advancing.
If the iterator reaches the logical end with an unterminated multiline string, this byte probe can step past the buffer and produce the reported global-buffer-overflow read.
